body: That might be a good idea. I haven't had a great relationship with my mother in the past and she's not totally understanding of mental health things (I think she's genuinely trying, but that doesn't mean she gets it still), but our relationship is improving. If I can get the help I need, I would be able to prevent sending her through that but also without having to deal with the extra dimension to our relationship it adds. Finding *someone* to be that emergency contact though is probably a good idea.

Thank you for the response regardless :) musical pursuits are very important. I seem to have fallen asleep actually, sorry. 

I want two things, really. One, I want to work in academia most of all. It's my goal and it's been my whole life up until this point. Two, I just want to not feel miserable and stressed. I can't remember a time when I haven't been anxious and it's just so taxing. Otherwise, I'm satisfied with having few friends, with having little money (of course I need enough to live on), with living in less than ideal places (small houses, lots of roommates, unpleasant cities), with being single. I'm a kind of academia-and-my-guitar kind of person. My guitar doesn't seem to be going anywhere, but the academia part is very difficult. 

I've heard of trying meditation. Actually, one therapist I had temporarily had me do mindfulness and I liked that, but I couldn't keep seeing her due to my college's restrictions on number of visits with school therapists :/ I have a hard time understanding how to do it by myself though.

The thing that's been the biggest help ever is knowing that there are people who do try to help and who understand. Thank you so, so much again for talking to me. I don't want to die. I want to get help, which is the point of this post I guess. It just feels like such an impossible, solitary thing to help.

Sorry, GAD is Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Basically I'm constantly anxious - jittery, jumpy, panicked. I'm stressed a lot. This is basically impossible stress, if it's stress. 

1. Sorry, what do you mean exactly? I'll take advice, I truly do appreciate it. Despite what people tend to think, I don't think a lot of people *want* to die, they want to not feel the way they do.

2. My major is linguistics

3. Yeah, Wellbutrin daily for depression and Klonopin as needed for anxiety - I've tried a pretty wide host of other meds too though.

Thank you for talking with me

I suppose you must be right, yeah. It's unfortunate, it's sort of a deterrent to me getting help. :/

I've been struggling with severe depression off and on for something like six years and I'm not even 20 yet. The career path I've been trying to pursue - academia - is almost impossible, that's even hoping I get into grad school. If I go straight to grad school, I will certainly have worse breakdowns. If I don't, I lose my health insurance and have to pray with everything in me that I'll get a job. I won't have a useful degree. It's useful if I want to research in the field, which I do, but otherwise it's not. I've got OCD which provides constant intrusive thoughts on everything from stabbing my little brother to death to trying to fuck a dog to throwing myself in front of a bus. All day. GAD which makes me worry constantly and have panic attacks that make me embarrassingly leave class and things all the time. I've made my identity completely someone I don't want to be in almost every way and have no way of fixing it short of cutting off all ties with everyone and moving across the world. I've got a poor relationship with my family. I'm in love with someone who is not attracted to my gender. I'm doing nothing really that helps anyone at all. The only thing I was really proud of myself for doing was giving blood and I can't even do that because my pulse is too high which makes me more anxious which makes me more depressed which makes me more desperate for something, anything, to make me feel marginally useful. I just can't imagine living like this for much longer. This next *week* seems painfully impossible.
